chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Muthannā al-Ḥannāṭ, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), and I said to him, "Are you the heirs of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?" He said, "Yes." I said, "The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the heir of the Prophets, and he knew all that they knew?" He said to me, "Yes." I said, "Then you are able to give life to the dead and cure the blind and the leper?" He said, "Yes, by the permission of Allah."

Then he said to me, "Come near to me, O Abū Muḥammad." So I came near him, and he wiped over my face and over my eyes, and I saw the sun, the sky, the earth, the houses, and everything in the town. Then he said to me, "Would you like to remain like this, with the same obligations and liabilities as the people upon the Day of Judgment, or return to how you were and have Paradise exclusively?" I said, "I return to how I was." So he wiped over my eyes, and I returned to how I was.
He said: Then I narrated this to Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, and he said, "I bear witness that this is true, just as the day is true."

key_terms.الْأَبْرَصَ: the leper, one afflicted with leprosy
key_terms.الْأَكْمَهَ: the blind, specifically one afflicted with blindness
key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: the Prophets, whose knowledge is described as inherited by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and then by the Imams
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: by the permission of Allah, indicating that such acts occur only through divine authorization
key_terms.تُبْرِئُوا: to cure or heal, referring to miraculous healing
key_terms.تُحْيُوا الْمَوْتَى: to give life to the dead, mentioned here as occurring by Allah’s permission
key_terms.وَرَثَةُ: heirs or inheritors, referring here to the inherited authority and knowledge of the Imams
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, the day of reckoning and accountability

ai.seo_question: Can the Imams, by Allah’s permission, perform miracles such as healing the blind and reviving the dead?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) as inheriting the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), who in turn inherited the knowledge of the Prophets. It also affirms, by the permission of Allah, extraordinary signs associated with the Imams, including healing and reviving the dead. The report further links such divine favor with accountability on the Day of Judgment and contrasts worldly capacity with the promise of Paradise.
